- Terrible environmental lighting, it's so bright that you will get instant headache after 5 minutes.
- Game looks like a blurry painting smeared with butter ( I'm running native resolution, no upscaling)
- No FOV slider support, on a Ultra wide (3440 x 1440) the screen looks 2D flat. Causing discomfort.
- Fixed camera, can't zoom in or offset the camera.

This game can be summed up as thus:

Valheim but some runescape elements like magical abilities, which adds a lot of flare and mechanics to your gameplay. There are also iconic items from the main game, and enemies that will have you getting flashbacks to times of old. In early stages of development now so there's not much content yet, but there is much potential for a really great game. Wouldn't recommend this trash to anyone.

After the first couple areas its a broken ,janky mess that constantly repeats the same points. All the fun is front loaded. Has potential, but should still be in EA for at least another year. Check back after a couple big updates, maybe they will fix it, not worth your time now.

This game is still in early access, and I noticed this even during character creation, where the hairstyles are named with numbers, for example.

According to the RuneScape Dragons Wild roadmap, it will be in early access for another year. That doesn't mean it's not worth playing! I'm only four hours in, but it's a blast! The beautiful graphics, combat, and skill system are smooth and fun.

It's been a long time since a game has hooked me like this! I'm looking forward to seeing where the game development is heading, and I'm rooting for the developers.

I feel like their development approach is similar to Satisfactory's. They want to release a strong, stable 1.0 version, which is uncommon in today's industry. The last game I played was New World, which was fond of releasing MVP (minimum viable product). The fact that they are gone now speaks for itself.

I wish the developers the best of luck, and I hope all the players have a good time in Ashenfall. :)

Truth be told, don't listen to the people yapping about "I've played Runescape for so long"... dude it's a different style. It's fun. Level progression among regions is fun if you're just an average gamer who likes to have playing after work or if you have free time on the weekends. It's a good game.

Onto the negatives:
Early levels seem kind of tough. Rats are killing you quick and cows are kicking your butt lol. It takes a couple hours until you can comfortably kill mobs in a quick succession. Not a big whoop. The game doesn't really help with crafting stuff... normal RS has a brilliant tutorial on how to use ores, silks, leathers, and bars to craft better armor.. etc. This game doesn't give that good of a guide about that.. beware.

Overall:
- Play it if you like to take your time, have fun, explore, and build.
- Do not play if you plan on griding for a weekend or two , telling your friends its fun, and never playing again, and then complaining about repetitiveness... just be normal and experience the game yourself.

I upgraded my PC so giving the game a second shot: The game is ... pretty okay. Very grindy, areas are big and fun to explore. Build diversity is not very good due to soulslike combat (which means you are always a glass cannon). Cool armor sets seem to only be available in the mid-to-late game.
A 5800X3D cpu and RX 9070XT really helped with getting stable 75FPS without framegen. Graphics are okay, lighting isn't the best and I have some visual artifacts inside Vaults. Sounds and music are good.
Building is fun. Resource gathering is pretty fun too. I like the art style.

Previously on On RTX 2080 paired with R9 3900X I found it unplayable with no way to stabilize FPS anywhere near 60. And taking a massive loss on quality is just not worth it on a big monitor.

I started playing during the early access release and instantly fell in love with the game. It began with minimal content, but the effort and passion was clearly visible. While not entirely a "RuneScape" game, it had just enough to hint without being overtly in your face about being a "RuneScape" game. 

Playing solo and with friends was a blast for the first few months! Once updates and quality of life changes were implemented- the game really did change. What was once a RuneScape themed Valheim look-a-like has grown into it's own niche and has truly recaptured what I felt the first time playing OSRS. I have not had this much enjoyment out of a game in a while. I am eagerly waiting on the new areas to come and can't wait to see how deep they can go with this game.

Fantastic work! Please, keep up the momentum!

To anyone who left when it was still new, you tele'd too early.

Honestly, this is the most fun I've ever had in a survival RPG. You will likely die... a LOT but the more you explore, the more you are rewarded. I've finished most of the content currently available and I've switched gears and started building a permanent base. The base building is very robust with more snap points than you can dream of. Skillful combat is also highly rewarding with the parry system.

I'd been debating on whether or not to buy RuneScape: Dragonwilds for awhile now. I'm put in about 500 hours in Enshrouded, but stopped playing after its 1.0 update in May, as the nerf to the gliding mechanic basically sucked the fun out of being mobile during heavy combat or trying to get out of the Shroud. I'd dabbled (barely played, maybe 4 hours) in Valheim, but its initial progression is very slow. So I bought Dragonwilds. I've not "looked back", it's been a lot of fun. Pretty easy to figure out (except the Rune Crafting, it was a bit confusing at first). It is definitely a slower paced game than Enshrouded, it's more like Valheim for its combat encounters, which is not necessarily a bad thing. I prefer more slower, meaningful encounters anyway versus obliterating mobs, rinse and repeat. It's fun to explore around, lots of hidden things. And the random raids keep you on your toes, along with the random dragon drive by attacks. I highly recommend RS:D for anyone who loves a good RPG/progression survival co-op (like these three games I've discussed), especially if you're an old school MMO/RPG player (e.g., Gen X, you know who you are). And, 1.0 is just around the corner, so it's a great time to get started!

The story is paper thin for RS standards *but* it is by far the best game of its kind I've played, the construction system is great. It does somehow capture the Runescape vibe, which is amazing. Great progression. 

Combat is being improved, Originally I was going to say it is quite boring but not really, it's just not super complex, which is not a bad thing.

Playing this game isn't like going to even McDonalds. You go 100 times nothing too bad, But one day you get a hair in your burger and try to raise it to their attention. Normally a manager would make sure to handle the situation. Playing Dragonwilds you're expected to eat your burger with hair in it because they're too busy releasing the latest Big Mac.

Valheim, Enshrouded, and Stardew Valley have a new sibling: RuneScape: Dragonwilds!

Satisfying progression, crafting, building, solid combat, and dragons. It delivers a fun and immersive adventure, especially for fans of survival games and fantasy RPGs.

But calling it an open-world game isn't entirely accurate. The world is big and feels alive, but it doesn't feel truly open. The game follows a linear progression, with certain quests required to access new areas. Still, that doesn't take away from all the fun this game has to offer.

10/10

Runescape stuff is fairly superficial which is good if you don't care for Runescape but not great if you wanted stuff to actually be Runescape. Game is kind of a slog still even with magic helping with some stuff. Combat is buns which I suppose is par for the course for survival crafting but for a game with so much combat having it be a bit more in depth and actually engaging would be nice. Maybe it's better with a larger group of people playing but as a solo player it leaves very little to enjoy and if a game relies on friends making it enjoyable then the game itself is fundamentally not enjoyable.

Goblin raids are way too frequent. and a very big annoyance if I'm just trying to let a friend play on my world while I'm doing chores.
You CAN turn them off, with the Major and Minor world event slider, but I can't find anything that specifies what a minor and major world event is exactly. Like is the Goblin raid/hunt a minor event, and the dragon flying over to attack a major event? or are both minor, and I just haven't seen a major?
There's other information online that states they are sometimes tied to quests as well, but there's absolutely nothing concrete. Just the most vague definitions possible.

Having some clarity on this would absolutely make the game more enjoyable, because right now what I'm able to gather is telling me I'll be missing out on content if I turn off the "annoy and interrupt me" feature.

Never could get in to og Runescape however, this game is amazing. Missing a few tiles for building but this is early access so there is more to come and obviously there are going to be bugs and crashes. I particularly enjoy the magic system requiring runes which (for the time being) doesn't take up inventory and encumbrance. Right now there is only fire and wind magic for combat use and I, in particular, can hardly wait for lightning to be introduced. I believe Dragonwilds has great potential and look forward to seeing its growth.

My only dislike, thus far, is the "body type" category in character creation. I thought, "Oh. I have choices to make my character short and fat, tall and lanky, fit, pear shaped..." you get the idea. Imagine my disappointment when type is actually related to male and female. Last I checked, body type and gender are different categories. Disappointing and misleading. Normally, I'd automatically down rate and get a refund but I haven't seen any blatantly forced political agenda that a lot of developers have been putting in these games recently so I'm keeping it a thumbs up.

Again, I look forward to seeing this game grow and officially launch with bated breath.
